The most likely corrupted element is the tail source **M5**. It is the only device whose current contradicts its mirror ratio, and it sits exactly at the saturation edge.

- **M5 headroom:** Vds = Vdsat = 0.176 V, so Vds−Vdsat = 0 V. Its tail node is fixed by the input common-mode level (0.9 V) minus the pair's Vgs (0.724 V), so it has no margin to absorb corners or temperature.
- **M5 current:** Its W/L ratio to M0 is 25.16, which should give about 250 uA. It carries only 226.7 uA, roughly 10% below that, consistent with the device being pushed toward triode.
- **Swing sensitivities:** M5 has the largest listed sensitivity, and the other listed sensitivities (Mb1, Mb2, M0) all act through the same tail and pb bias chain.

The triode condition on M10/M11 (Vds 0.191 V vs Vdsat 0.213 V) is a symptom of the NMOS stack and is identical in both devices. A single fault cannot produce two identical symptoms, so these are secondary. Mb2 and Mb1 follow as the next candidates because they set the pb bias that feeds the tail mirror and the PMOS loads.
